text:
jess: FYI — several customers hitting 502/504s from hosted inference since ~09:12 UTC. Gateway shows spikes of upstream timeouts and a lot of cache auth failures. sample req id: req-9a2f7b.

michael: ugh. which endpoint? embeddings or generation? any quick logs?

jess: primarily text.generate (/v1/completions). pasted gateway snippet:
```
2026-03-17T09:12:08Z gateway INFO req=req-9a2f7b upstream_timeout=10000ms backend=hosted-inference-1 error="GET memcached:AUTH failed"
2026-03-17T09:12:09Z gateway WARN req=req-9a2f7c kv_prefix_miss=true fallback_to_db=true
2026-03-17T09:12:10Z gateway ERROR req=req-9a2f7d upstream=hosted-inference-1 status=504 reason="pool_exhausted; memcached auth error"
```

riya: escalating to eng-sre, collecting affected customer list and repro. looks like memcached/redis auth flapping + hotspot on a small prefix.

srebot: Pager created INC-2026 — paging oncall-sre. Priority: high.

carmen: oncall here. Seeing auth failures from memcached proxies to the auth service (KMS token rotation job scheduled at 09:10 UTC). Logs show a handful of nodes that started rejecting auth and then got marked unhealthy, which caused heavy fallthrough to upstream inference nodes and then queueing/timeouts.

jess: customers reporting user-facing timeouts and retries, some billing alerts firing. Can we do a quick mitigation (bypass cache for hosted gateway) while we fix auth?

carmen: yes. I'll flip bypass for the affected prefix group to stop backend pressure. Run admin call:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://admin.redwood.internal/feature_flags/cache_bypass \
  -d '{"prefix":"v1-emb-*","duration_s":900,"reason":"memcached_auth_flap"}'
```

carmen: doing that now... :wrench:

carmen: bypass applied. monitoring metrics.

michael: status page draft: "We are experiencing elevated 5xx rates for hosted inference due to a cache dependency auth issue. Engineers are actively investigating and we have temporarily bypassed cache for affected traffic to reduce errors." Any edits?

riya: looks good. add ETA: initial mitigation in place, investigating root cause.

carmen: after bypass, error rate dropped ~85% in 2m, backend latency back to normal. Memcached cluster still showing auth rejections on 3/12 proxies. We're rolling back the KMS token rotation that started at 09:10 and restarting proxy connectors one-by-one to re-establish sessions.

jess: can we capture repro steps and a minimal trace for postmortem? I ran a curl that reproduces the 504 when cache is active:
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","prompt":"test","max_tokens":10}'
# when cache auth broken, response 504 with body: {"error":"upstream timeout (cache fallback->backend)"}
```

carmen: saved. also grabbed debug from memcached proxies:
```
[09:11:59] proxy-7 ERROR auth_check failed status=401 token=stale
[09:12:01] proxy-8 WARN reconnecting to auth-service (timeout)
[09:12:05] proxy-9 INFO marked_unhealthy reason=auth_fail
[09:13:20] proxy-7 INFO rejoined cluster
```

riya: customers notified via status page and support tickets updated. couple asked for credit, capturing for billing followup.

carmen: root cause so far: KMS/token rotation job issued new creds but didn't update a subset of proxy connectors (hotspot on specific prefix hashed to those proxies). That caused auth thrashing and partial cluster outage -> fallthrough -> gateway queueing -> 5xx. We'll add a safer rolling update and health gating on rotations.

michael: can we add a temporary rule to limit prefix hashing to spread load? also add alert to detect auth error ratio before failover to DB.

carmen: agreed. put action items in INC: add circuit-breaker threshold and detect auth error spike. Also add a playbook note for immediate bypass.

jess: customer A confirmed recovery and no more 504s after 09:19 UTC. closing loop. thanks everyone. :tada:

riya: will file postmortem and billing followup. tagging this thread in INC-2026.

srebot: Incident INC-2026 status -> mitigated, monitoring.
